page: Amazon Web Services r8ib.24xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance runs on an x86_64 Intel processor operating at 3.9 GHz. Compute resources comprise 48 physical cores, providing 96 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core. System memory totals 768.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU allocation designed for large data sets in memory.

The instance does not include bundled local instance storage and operates with zero local NVMe or SSD disks, requiring remote network storage such as EBS for persistent data. Hardware accelerators are absent, with a GPU count of zero. Network connectivity is a primary feature of the configuration, offering a baseline throughput of 100 Gbps for high-bandwidth data transfers and cluster communications.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8ib.24xlarge consolidates extensive memory arrays and high-capacity network interfaces into a single node. The architecture eliminates local storage hardware overhead, focusing investment on memory capacity and network throughput. However, workloads requiring fast local scratch disks will need to utilize network-attached volumes, introducing potential network overhead for disk I/O.

This server profile fits memory-intensive applications requiring substantial RAM alongside enterprise network performance. Typical use cases include large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, big data analytics clusters, and high-concurrency enterprise applications.
